key_insight: The paper develops a dimension-efficient neural network approximation theory for fractional parabolic PDEs by separating temporal and spatial regularity in anisotropic spectral Barron spaces.
engineering_relevance: This provides a principled path to train two-layer networks that approximate time-dependent fractional diffusion models with dimension-independent error control.
method: Build anisotropic spectral Barron spaces that measure time and space regularity separately in frequency space.
Prove dimension-independent maximal regularity using multiplication estimates and the method of continuity for drift and potential terms.
Use a Vandermonde-based global-in-time extension of the fractional heat semigroup to analyze forward evolution and derive approximation bounds.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical approximation bounds, including n^{-1/2} rates in mixed Sobolev norms for periodic activations and, under extra anisotropic Barron regularity, for certain non-periodic activations.
watch_item: The uniform-in-time spectral Barron regularity can fail in general, so the theory may not transfer to all time horizons without additional assumptions.
paper_title: Neural Network Approximation of Solutions to Fractional Parabolic Partial Differential Equations
